Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving this through our clinical platform team and procurement — initial ask from engineering is a recommended sizing for a dedicated/private deployment for evaluation. Key constraints:
- Target steady-state throughput: ~120 inference requests/sec (avg 512 tokens per request, 8k context spikes for some flows)
- Regions: US-East primary, EU-West as DR/replication
- Prefer H100 or A100 80GB; open to a mixed pool if recommended
- Timeline: 6 week evaluation window; procurement wants a clear MAP and kickoff date

Can you send a quick MAP-style plan with owner names, estimated GPU mix/count, throughput targets (p50/p95 latencies), and procurement milestones? Procurement is looped on this email.

Jenna

Subject: RE: Sizing guidance — dedicated/private deployment

Jenna — thanks, this is helpful. Draft MAP and quick sizing notes below; attaching Acme_MAP_v3.xlsx with the week-by-week owner table. High level proposal:

Summary proposal (initial POC -> evaluation -> scale):
- Phase 1 (Week 0–2): POC — validate throughput & latency on representative workload
  - US-East: 2 x H100 (80GB) dedicated nodes, model shard + KV cache; target 120 req/s steady, p95 <= 350ms for 512-token avg
  - EU-West: 1 x A100 (80GB) in passive replica mode (DR) with perf testing windows; target 30 req/s steady p95 <= 420ms
- Phase 2 (Week 3–4): Extended evaluation — increase concurrency and run failure/fallover tests
  - Add 2x H100 burst capacity (on standby) if sustained CPU/GPU utilization > 85% during tests
- Phase 3 (Week 5–6): Close / roll into reserved capacity — finalize SKU commit and SLAs

Owners (high level):
- Soojin Lee (Redwood) — MAP lead, technical coordinator, ensures infra build + kickoff
- Marissa Cole (Redwood) — capacity planning & cost estimates
- Rishi Malhotra (Redwood) — latency/QA validation and perf sign-off
- Jenna Ortiz (Acme) — product/acceptance criteria owner

Immediate action items:
- (SoJ-01) Share MAP spreadsheet (attached) and HubSpot record for Jenna/procurement — owner: Soojin — due: 2026-11-25
- (Mar-01) Produce a GPU-mix cost delta (H100 vs A100) and expected token cost — owner: Marissa — due: 2026-11-26
- (Rish-01) Run a latency sweep on representative traces and report p50/p95 targets — owner: Rishi — due: 2026-11-27

Notes on performance assumptions:
- Model profile used: 70B open-checkpoint variant (KV cache enabled) — continuous batching expected to give 1.8–2.1x throughput improvement over naïve single-request runs for 512-token avg
- For 8k context spikes we recommend transient increase of KV memory and short-lived shard capacity (burst nodes) to avoid p95 spikes

Attachments: Acme_MAP_v3.xlsx (MAP timeline + owner matrix)
Related link: HubSpot deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/ACM-2026-0934

Happy to sync live — propose short kickoff 30m on Monday the 29th.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing guidance — dedicated/private deployment (GPU mix + cost)

Adding a couple of concrete SKU suggestions and cost notes for the MAP spreadsheet. I also attached a quick throughput_modeling.csv with the test vectors Marissa used.

Suggested GPU mix (final recommendation):
- US-East primary: 4 x H100 (80GB) split across 2 rack-isolated nodes (2 H100 each) — baseline for steady 120 req/s with room for burst. If budget constrained, 3 x H100 might work with more aggressive batching but higher p95 risk.
- EU-West DR: 2 x A100 (80GB) in warm-standby (replicated KV) — can ramp to active for regional testing

Throughput targets (test validation):
- US-East: steady 120 req/s, p50 ~ 85ms, p95 <= 350ms (512 tokens)
- For 8k context spike tests: maintain p95 <= 1.2s with burst nodes engaged

Cost delta (rough): H100 pool (4 units) approximates 1.9x the monthly reserved cost of 4x A100 for equivalent token volume. Exact numbers in MAP sheet.

Action for Rishi: please validate the p95 numbers on the attached traces and flag any model-level ops that could push p95 over 500ms under concurrency.

Attachments: throughput_modeling.csv, SLA_draft.pdf

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
